newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: U.S. helps Cambodia curb human trafficking.
newsitem.headline: U.S. helps Cambodia curb human trafficking.

text.p: The United States is helping Cambodia clamp down on the stream of illegal aliens using the Southeast Asian nation as a transit point for migration to America and other nations.

"We understand the illegal movement of people is now one of the greatest problems our two countries face," Ambassador Kenneth Quinn on Wednesday told some of the 100 immigration officials gathered for U.S.-sponsored training in detecting false travel documents.
"There are people who want to take advantage of Cambodia and use it for the illegal movement of people, and there are people who want to take advantage of the United States," he added.
The embassy said the two-day training course would help Cambodian authorities detect fake documents used by smugglers of illegal aliens, drug traffickers and others involved in organised crime.
The United States provided 50 ultraviolet lights to help identify fake or altered passports, officials said, noting Cambodia's growing status as a haven for human smuggling rings.

"Cambodia has become the transit point for the movement of illegal aliens not just to the United States but obviously other countries also," said Ralph Folester of the U.S. Immigration Service, one of three officials conducting the course.
He said smugglers from Cambodia found it a convenient staging point for their syndicates, which then transport people throughout Asia and the Americas.
"The cost is no object. The cost of moving these individuals is anything from $15,000 to $30,000," he said, noting the illegal aliens faced lives of servitude to pay off their travel costs.
Folester recalled a case in December when Cambodian police arrested three suspected triad gang members and 78 illegal Chinese immigrants in a villa in Phnom Penh.
They found a notebook with crime contacts throughout Europe, Africa and the Americas.
